sample_unit: patient-trial eligibility determinations in expert-adjudicated gold corpus (plus 55 in manual screening comparison)

links.outcome: Sensitivity in identifying truly eligible patients: adapted TrialGPT versus manual screening
links.effect: System identified more than twice as many truly eligible patients than manual screening (81.8% vs 36.4%) with equivalent specificity, n = 55.
links.quote: Compared with manual screening, it identified more than twice as many truly eligible patients (81.8% vs 36.4%) while preserving equivalent specificity.

links.outcome: Local performance against expert-adjudicated reference standard
links.effect: Against the expert-adjudicated corpus (n = 149): 81.8% sensitivity, 97.8% specificity, PPV 75.0%.
links.quote: Against the expert-adjudicated corpus, the system achieved 81.8% sensitivity, 97.8% specificity, and a positive predictive value of 75.0%.

unlisted_practices: Locally hosted LLM for secure deployment with PHI
Restructuring inputs as longitudinal patient-encounter-note hierarchy mirroring EHR documentation

screen.reason: The study evaluates a locally deployed LLM adaptation (TrialGPT) for clinical trial eligibility screening against an expert gold standard and manual screening on retrospective/validation cohorts, but does not test specific deployment practices or guardrails.
